Rashi on Nedarim 54a:1:1.english: One who vows [that] vegetables [are forbidden to him], etc., and Rabbi Akiva prohibits - For he holds [that] gourds [are] included in [the category of] vegetables.

Rashi on Nedarim 54a:1:2.english: Only gourds - [This] implies that [a gourd] is not of its kind.

Rashi on Nedarim 54a:2:1.hebrew: לא מצאתי אלא קיטנית - בתמיה. כלומר, להכי לא קאמר ליה אלא די דילועין, מכלל דדילועין מיניה הוא ולא מין קיטנית:
Rashi on Nedarim 54a:2:1.english: I found only legumes - [This is asked] rhetorically. That is to say, that is why [the agent] only says to him [that] of gourds, [which proves] by implication that gourds are of [the same] kind as [vegetables], and not a kind of legume.

Rashi on Nedarim 54a:2:2.english: Fresh Egyptian bean - [It] is a type of vegetable.

Rashi on Nedarim 54a:2:3.english: And [it is] permitted [when] dry - For it is a kind of grain.

Rashi on Nedarim 54a:3:1.hebrew: אמאי אוסר ר"ע, הא מן ירק נדר - ודילועין לא איקרי ירק:
Rashi on Nedarim 54a:3:1.english: Why does Rabbi Akiva prohibit [gourds]? Didn't he vow from vegetables? - And gourds are not called vegetables.

Rashi on Nedarim 54a:3:2.hebrew: ירקי קדרה עלי - ודילועין בכלל ירקי קדרה הן, שהרי מתבשלין בקדרה:
Rashi on Nedarim 54a:3:2.english: Vegetables of a pot [are forbidden] to me - And gourds are included in [the category of] vegetables of a pot, for they are cooked in a pot.

Rashi on Nedarim 54a:3:3.hebrew: ודילמא - האי דקאמר ירקי קדרה עלי, ירק הנאכל בקדרה עלי קאמר, כגון שומים ובצלים, שהן נאכלים בקדרה, שנותנין אותן בקדרה כדי ליתן טעם בתבשיל:
Rashi on Nedarim 54a:3:3.english: And perhaps - [when] this [person] says, "Vegetables of a pot [are forbidden] to me," he means, "A vegetable that is eaten in a pot [is forbidden] to me," such as garlic and onions, which are eaten in a pot, as they put them in a pot in order to give flavor to a cooked dish.

Rashi on Nedarim 54a:3:4.hebrew: באומר ירק המתבשל בקדרה - דדילועין נמי הן מתבשלין בקדרה, ונותנין אותן בשביל תבשיל. אבל שומין אין נותנין אותן אלא בשביל טעם, ולהכי ר"ע אוסר:
Rashi on Nedarim 54a:3:4.english: [Referring] to one who says, "A vegetable that is cooked in a pot" - For gourds are also cooked in a pot, and are put in for [the sake of being] a cooked dish. Garlic, however, is only put in for flavor, and therefore Rabbi Akiva prohibits [gourds].

Rashi on Nedarim 54a:4:1.hebrew: דצריך שלוחא לאימלוכי עליה - כגון דילועין: כי אמר לשלוחו קח לי ירק, אינו מביא לו דילועין, אלא אומר לו: לא מצאתי אלא דילועין, ומימליך עליה וקאמר ליה דרוצה אתה שאביא לך דילועין. וכהאי גוונא לאו מיניה, לפיכך כי נדר בירק, מותר בדילועין:
Rashi on Nedarim 54a:4:1.english: That an agent must consult about it - For example, gourds: when [one] says to his agent, "Buy me vegetables," [the agent] does not bring him gourds, but rather says to him, "I found only gourds," and consults with him, saying to him, "[Do] you want me to bring you gourds?" And such a case is not [considered] the same type; therefore, when one vows [not to benefit] from vegetables, he is permitted [to eat] gourds.

Rashi on Nedarim 54a:4:2.hebrew: ורבי עקיבא סבר כו' - מדקאמר ליה "לא מצאתי אלא דילועין" ולא אמר "לא מצאתי אלא קיטנית", אלמא דילועין מין ירק הוא:
Rashi on Nedarim 54a:4:2.english: And Rabbi Akiva maintains, etc. - Since [the agent] said to him, "I found only gourds," and did not say, "I found only legumes," it follows that gourds are a type of vegetable.

Rashi on Nedarim 54a:4:3.hebrew: מודה רבי עקיבא - אע"ג דאוסר בדילועין, אם אכל דילועין אינו לוקה, דקסבר ליכא מלקות דלא יחל דברו, הואיל וצריך לאימלוכי ביה עלה:
Rashi on Nedarim 54a:4:3.english: Rabbi Akiva concedes - Even though [Rabbi Akiva] prohibits [gourds], if he ate gourds he is not flogged, for he holds [that] there are no lashes for "he shall not profane his word," since [an agent] must consult with him about it.

Rashi on Nedarim 54a:6:1.hebrew: מתניתין - דמעילה דשליח מעל, דלא כר"ע, דקתני סיפא: לא עשה שליחותו, שליח מעל:
Rashi on Nedarim 54a:6:1.english: The Mishnah - [meaning the Mishnah] of [Tractate] Me'ilah, [which states] that the agent committed misuse [of consecrated property], is not in accordance with Rabbi Akiva, as the latter clause teaches: "[If] he did not carry out his agency, the agent committed misuse [of consecrated property]."

Rashi on Nedarim 54a:6:2.hebrew: אמר לשלוחו תן בשר לאורחים ונתן להם כבד שליח מעל - דלא עשה שליחותו, דאין כבד בכלל בשר:
Rashi on Nedarim 54a:6:2.english: [If] he said to his agent, "Give meat to the guests," and he gave them liver, the agent has committed misuse [of consecrated property] - Because he did not fulfill his agency, as liver is not included in [the category of] meat.

Rashi on Nedarim 54a:6:3.hebrew: ואי ר"ע - הא אמר כבד בכלל בשר הוי, דמילתא דמימליך עלה שליח מיניה הוא. וה"נ, אע"ג דלא אימליך השתא, אורחיה הוא לאימלוכי, דכי אמר לו "תן בשר לאורחין" ולא היה לו בשר אלא כבד, דרכו לומר "אין לי אלא כבד", וכמאן דמימליך דמי:
Rashi on Nedarim 54a:6:3.english: And if [it were] Rabbi Akiva - Behold, he said [that] liver is included in meat, for any matter about which an agent consults is [considered] of the same type. And here too, even though he did not consult [the employer] now, it is his way to consult [about it], for when [the employer] says to him, "Give meat to the guests," and he has no meat, only liver, it is his way to say, "I have only liver," and it is as though he consulted [him].

Rashi on Nedarim 54a:6:4.english: Let the homeowner be liable for misuse - For [the agent] fulfilled his agency.

Tosafot on Nedarim 54a:1:1.hebrew: הנודר מן הירק אסור בדילועין - והוא אומר "לא מצאתי אלא דלועין" - ואין לוקחם מיד, אלמא לא קרי להו אינשי ירק:
Tosafot on Nedarim 54a:1:1.english: "One who vows [to abstain] from vegetables is prohibited from gourds" - And he says, "I found only gourds" — and he does not buy them immediately, [indicating that] people do not call them vegetables.

Tosafot on Nedarim 54a:2:1.english: He said to them: The matter is so - That is to say, from there I bring a proof.

Tosafot on Nedarim 54a:2:2.english: "[It] is prohibited [to eat] the cowpea" - For according to everyone, it is included in [the category of] vegetables.

Tosafot on Nedarim 54a:2:3.english: And [it is] permitted [when] dry - For it is not called a vegetable.

Tosafot on Nedarim 54a:3:1.hebrew: והא מן ירק נדר - ולמה אסור בדלועין, שהם פירי:
Tosafot on Nedarim 54a:3:1.english: And didn't he vow [to abstain] from vegetables? - And why is he prohibited [from eating] gourds, which are fruit?

Tosafot on Nedarim 54a:3:2.hebrew: באומר ירקי קדירה עלי - כשדרכם לבשלם, והני דרכם לבשלם:
Tosafot on Nedarim 54a:3:2.english: [Referring] to one who says, "Vegetables of a pot [are forbidden] to me" - [Meaning,] when it is customary to cook them, and these [gourds] — it is customary to cook them.

Tosafot on Nedarim 54a:3:3.hebrew: ודלמא ירק הנאכל בקדירה קאמר - כגון שומין ובצלים, שהוא נאכל בקדירה, כגון ליתן טעם בתבשיל:
Tosafot on Nedarim 54a:3:3.english: And perhaps he is saying: A vegetable that is eaten in a pot - For example, garlic and onions, which are eaten in a pot, such as to give flavor to a cooked dish.

Tosafot on Nedarim 54a:3:4.hebrew: באומר ירק המתבשל בקדירה - מפני שהוא קשה, וקסבר ר"ע דלועין בכלל ירק המתבשלים בקדירה:
Tosafot on Nedarim 54a:3:4.english: To one who says, "A vegetable that is cooked in a pot" - [This refers to a gourd,] because it is hard [and requires cooking], and Rabbi Akiva holds that gourds are included in [the category of] "vegetables that are cooked in a pot."

Tosafot on Nedarim 54a:4:1.english: And [an agent] needs to consult - For he does not buy them without specification until he consults about it.

Tosafot on Nedarim 54a:4:2.hebrew: מודה הוא לענין מלקות - בל יחל, שאינו לוקה, דמספקא ליה אי דלועין בכלל ירק, ומספיקא [לא] אמר למילקיה:
Tosafot on Nedarim 54a:4:2.english: He concedes with regard to lashes - [i.e., lashes for] bal yachel [violating a vow], that he is not flogged, because he is uncertain whether gourds are included in vegetables, and out of doubt one does [not] say to flog him.

Tosafot on Nedarim 54a:5:1.english: We learned there - [In] the last chapter of Me'ilah (20a).

Tosafot on Nedarim 54a:5:2.hebrew: בעה"ב מעל - דגמרינן "חטא חטא" מתרומה: מה התם ע"י שליח, אף הכא ע"י שליח, אע"ג דבעלמא אין שליח לדבר עבירה:
Tosafot on Nedarim 54a:5:2.english: The employer misused [the consecrated item] - For we derive [a gezerah shavah of] "sin, sin" from terumah: just as there [with terumah, it takes effect] through an agent, so too here [with me'ilah, it takes effect] through an agent, even though generally there is no agency for a transgression.

Tosafot on Nedarim 54a:6:1.hebrew: ונתן להם כבד - דכבד לאו מין בשר, וכי אמר לשלוחו "קח לי בשר" ולא מצא אלא כבד — לא מימליך עליה; וכששולחו לבקש בשר, אינו חוזר ואומר "לא מצאתי אלא כבד", אלא אומר "לא מצאתי בשר כלל":
Tosafot on Nedarim 54a:6:1.english: And he gave them liver - For liver is not a type of meat, and when one says to his agent, "Buy me meat," and he finds only liver, he does not consult [the sender] about it; and when he sends him to look for meat, he does not return and say, "I found only liver," rather he says, "I did not find meat at all."

Tosafot on Nedarim 54a:6:2.hebrew: מיניה הוא - ועשה שליחותו, ולמעול בעה"ב. וקשה, דרבי עקיבא מודה דאין לוקה, דמספקא ליה אי מידי דמימליך עליה מיניה הוא. ונראה דלא קשה כלל, דדוקא בדלועין — דלאו ירק הוא אלא פירי — מספקא ליה, אבל במידי אחרינא פשיטא ליה דמימליך עליה ומיניה הוא. וי"מ דהיינו הא דמשני: "מי לא מודה ר"ע דצריך לאימלוכי ביה?" — ומן הדין הוא דאינו מינו, ולהחמיר אר"ע [דמינו הוא], אבל לא למעול, דהאמר לעיל שאינו לוקה. ול"נ, דא"כ שליח אמאי מעל? כיון דמספקא ליה אם מינו [הוי או] אינו מינו, א"כ עשה שליחותו! ולכ"נ דודאי הפירוש כך הוא: "מי לא מודה ר"ע דצריך לימלוכי ביה?" — דבסתם אין השליח לוקח אם אין שואל למשלח אם יחפוץ; הילכך במעילה, כיון דשליח לא נמלך, לא הוי עשה שליחותו, ולכך מעל השליח כי נמי הוי מינו לגמרי. וקושיא ד"למעול בעה"ב" נתרץ בע"ה כמו שפירשתי. והר"ם היה אומר ד"למעול בעל הבית" לאו דוקא, אלא כלומר: לא ימעול שליח, וכדפרישית דשמא עשה שליחותו; ומשני: לא מודה דצריך לאימלוכי, כדפרישית:
Tosafot on Nedarim 54a:6:2.english: "It is of its kind" - and [thus] he fulfilled his agency, so let the householder be liable for misuse [of consecrated property]. And it is difficult, for Rabbi Akiva concedes that one does not receive lashes, because he is in doubt whether something about which [an agent] consults is of its kind. And it appears that it is not difficult at all, for specifically with gourds — which are not a vegetable, but a fruit — is he in doubt; whereas with other things, it is obvious to him that [an agent] consults about it and it is of its kind. And some explain that this is what [the Gemara] answers: "Does Rabbi Akiva not concede that one must consult about it?" — and by law it is not of its kind, and [only] to be stringent did Rabbi Akiva say [that it is of its kind], but not to be liable for misuse, for he said above that he does not receive lashes. And this does not appear [correct], for if so, why did the agent commit misuse? Since he is in doubt whether [it is] of its kind or not of its kind, if so, he [may have] fulfilled his agency! Therefore, it appears that certainly the explanation is thus: "Does Rabbi Akiva not concede that one must consult about it?" — for ordinarily an agent does not take [an item] unless he asks the sender if he wants [it]; therefore, regarding misuse, since the agent did not consult, it is not [considered that] he fulfilled his agency, and therefore the agent committed misuse even though it is completely of its kind. And the difficulty of "let the householder commit misuse" we will resolve, with God's help, as I explained. And the Ram [Rabbeinu Meir] used to say that "let the householder commit misuse" is not exact, rather it means: let the agent not commit misuse, as I explained, because perhaps he fulfilled his agency; and [the Gemara] answers: Does he not concede that one must consult, as I explained.
